findings.summary: Silent shortcut asserts a terminate without verifying the non-silent `list` rule will actually consume the line
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode (lines 182-191) purely on the shape of the line, bypassing the stock rule entirely. If the real `list` rule then declines non-silently on that same line (markdown-it's list.mjs has non-silent-applicable early returns, e.g. the `state.listIndent >= 0 && state.sCount[startLine] - state.listIndent >= 4 && state.sCount[startLine] < state.blkIndent` guard, and the 4-space indent guard), the paragraph has already been split and the bullet falls through to the paragraph rule as a literal one-line `-`. I could not construct a concrete input that reaches this (node_modules is not installed in the worktree, and `isEmptyBulletLine` requires `sCount >= blkIndent`), so this is a suspicion — but the two decisions (silent vs non-silent) are not kept in sync by construction, which is the fragile part.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__`; a dependency bump can throw at module init
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` (lines 207-214) casts `md.block.ruler` to expose the private `__rules__` array and throws `markdown-it block rule not found: list` if the shape changes. Because `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is applied at module scope in preview.ts:48, any such change turns into a throw at import time of the notes preview module (killing the whole notes view), not a degraded render. markdown-it is pinned as `^14.1.0`, so a minor/patch bump is picked up automatically. Similarly, the hand-copied `lheadingRule` will silently diverge from upstream on any 14.x change to lheading.

findings.summary: `asciiTrim` is not equivalent to upstream lheading's `.trim()`
findings.evidence: markdown-it 14's lheading computes `state.getLines(...).trim()`. `.trim()` strips all Unicode whitespace (NBSP U+00A0, U+2028, BOM, ...), whereas the local `asciiTrim` (lines 19-23) only strips the six ASCII whitespace chars. Heading content with leading/trailing non-ASCII whitespace will therefore differ from stock markdown-it output. Cosmetic, but the comment at line 17-18 asserts equivalence that does not hold.

findings.summary: Fix is broader than issue #517: single-dash setext headings are disabled everywhere, not just inside lists
findings.evidence: The `isLoneDash` guard in the replacement `lheading` rule (and `wrappedList`'s silent short-circuit, which only checks `state.parentType === 'paragraph'`) applies to *any* paragraph followed by a lone `-`, including at top level and inside blockquotes. So plain prose like `Heading\n-` — a perfectly ordinary, valid CommonMark h2 — now renders as a paragraph plus an empty bullet list, even though issue #517 is specifically about an *indented, nested* empty bullet under a list item. The design-doc note (docs/design/notes/notes.md:294-299) documents the broad rule as intentional, but the issue's outcome only asks for the nested-bullet case; narrowing the guard to `state.blkIndent > 0` / list context would satisfy the issue without removing a standard markdown feature. Note the added test only covers the multi-dash `---` form (`preview.test.ts:187`), so the single-dash regression is unasserted.

findings.summary: Reaches into markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry; a public `Ruler.before`/`push` approach avoids it
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: … }` to read a rule function, and `Ruler.at('list', …, { alt: [...] })` then has to hand-restore the rule's alt chain because the private replacement wipes it. Both couplings are avoidable: registering a small new block rule before `list` with `alt: ['paragraph']` uses only public API and leaves the stock `list`/`lheading` rules (and their alt chains) intact. Design-taste, but it is the fragile seam a markdown-it bump will break.

findings.summary: lheading was reimplemented wholesale but `=` (h1) underlines are untested
findings.evidence: lheadingRule re-creates the whole upstream rule, including the `EQUALS` branch that sets `level = 1` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:96-109), the >=4-space code-block guard (line 76), the lazy-continuation `continue` (line 84) and the terminator-rule loop (lines 118-127). findings.summary: Untested branches of the wrapped `list` rule: `*`/`+` empty bullets and the restored blockquote/reference alt contexts
findings.evidence: isEmptyBulletLine explicitly accepts `*` and `+` markers (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:40-42) and the wrapper is registered with `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` (lines 199-201), a chain the author notes must be restored by hand or `list` stops terminating those constructs. findings.summary: Editor syntax highlighting (@codemirror/lang-markdown) still treats a lone `-` as a setext underline, so the editor pane now disagrees with the preview pane
findings.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200` installs `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (imported at editor.ts:8), whose Lezer grammar follows CommonMark and will keep highlighting the `- 1` line of `- 1\n  -` as a SetextHeading. The preview, after this change, renders it as a nested list item. The two panes are shown side by side by the same `NoteEditor`, so users see the parent line styled as a heading while the preview shows a bullet. No code outside the diff was updated to keep the editor's markdown dialect in sync; a `markdownLanguage` config or an accepted-divergence note is needed.

findings.summary: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` passes no options, which resets `lheading`'s `alt` chain to `[]`
findings.evidence: `Ruler.at` sets `alt = options.alt || []` (the branch's own lessons file states this at docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:17-20, and the diff restores `alt` explicitly for `list` for exactly that reason). Line 175 replaces `lheading` with no options at all. Upstream markdown-it 14 registers `lheading` with no alt list, so this is most likely a no-op — but `node_modules` is not installed in this worktree so I could not confirm against `markdown-it/lib/parser_block.mjs`. If upstream ever gives `lheading` an alt entry, setext headings would stop terminating paragraphs/blockquotes/lists. Passing the upstream options back explicitly (as done for `list`) removes the doubt. Fix belongs on the new code.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex is quadratic (ReDoS) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing markdown-it's linear native `.trim()`
findings.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (lines 19-20) is applied via `asciiTrim(...)` at line 134 to the ENTIRE paragraph body of every setext heading the replaced `lheading` rule accepts. The trailing alternative `[ws]+$` used with the `g` flag is the classic quadratic `/\s+$/` shape (cf. Django CVE-2019-14232): for each start index inside a whitespace run the engine greedily consumes the run, fails `$` on the following non-whitespace char, and backtracks one char at a time, so cost is O(n^2) in the run length. Vector: a workspace member saves note content `"a" + " ".repeat(200000) + "b\n==="` (or `\n---`). Every collaborator whose preview renders that note — packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165, `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)`, synchronous on the UI thread — burns roughly 2e10 backtracking steps and the tab freezes, a stored denial of service that persists until the text is removed, needing only write access to shared note content. Upstream markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses native `.trim()` at this exact spot, which is linear, so the regression is introduced by this diff; the comment's claim that it re-creates "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`" does not justify the quadratic form. Fix: use `str.trim()` or a two-pointer index scan instead of a scanning regex. I could not execute markdown-it here (no node_modules in the worktree) to time the hang, hence medium confidence on exploitability; high confidence on the regex shape and that it runs on attacker-controlled content.

samples.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex is quadratic (ReDoS) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing markdown-it's linear native `.trim()`
samples.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (lines 19-20) is applied via `asciiTrim(...)` at line 134 to the ENTIRE paragraph body of every setext heading the replaced `lheading` rule accepts. The trailing alternative `[ws]+$` used with the `g` flag is the classic quadratic `/\s+$/` shape (cf. Django CVE-2019-14232): for each start index inside a whitespace run the engine greedily consumes the run, fails `$` on the following non-whitespace char, and backtracks one char at a time, so cost is O(n^2) in the run length. Vector: a workspace member saves note content `"a" + " ".repeat(200000) + "b\n==="` (or `\n---`). Every collaborator whose preview renders that note — packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165, `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(markdown)`, synchronous on the UI thread — burns roughly 2e10 backtracking steps and the tab freezes, a stored denial of service that persists until the text is removed, needing only write access to shared note content. Upstream markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses native `.trim()` at this exact spot, which is linear, so the regression is introduced by this diff; the comment's claim that it re-creates "markdown-it's own `asciiTrim`" does not justify the quadratic form. Fix: use `str.trim()` or a two-pointer index scan instead of a scanning regex. I could not execute markdown-it here (no node_modules in the worktree) to time the hang, hence medium confidence on exploitability; high confidence on the regex shape and that it runs on attacker-controlled content.
